verses.zh: 城墙修完，我安了门扇，守门的、歌唱的，和利未人都已派定。
verses.en: When the wall had been rebuilt and I had positioned the doors, and the gatekeepers, the singers, and the Levites had been appointed,
verses.commentary:
7:1 "the gatekeepers and the singers and the Levites" Some scholars see this as misplaced because it seems
to refer to the temple and not the city. Yet, we learn later, that the Levitical gatekeepers were also appointed
to the city gates because of the lack of people willing to live in Jerusalem (cf. Neh. 7:4).

verses.zh: 我就派我的弟兄哈拿尼和营楼的宰官哈拿尼雅管理耶路撒冷；因为哈拿尼雅是忠信的，又敬畏　神过于众人。
verses.en: I then put in charge over Jerusalem[NOTE:1] my brother Hanani and Hananiah[NOTE:2] the chief of the citadel, for he was a faithful man and feared God more than many do.
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

Some have suggested that “Hananiah” is another name for Hanani, Nehemiah’s brother, so that only one individual is mentioned here. However, the third person plural in v. 3 indicates two people are in view.
verses.commentary:
7:2 "I put Hanani my brother, and Hananiah" These could be two forms of one name (cf. BDB 337); both mean
"YHWH has been gracious." However, in Neh. 7:3 it says, "I said to them" which confirms that there were two men
involved. Hanani is first mentioned in Neh. 1:2 as Nehemiah's brother and source of his information about the
condition of Jerusalem. The name Hananiah also appears in the list of Neh. 10:23.

▣ "the commander of the fortress" Most walled cities had an inner fortress. "Fortress" is also used to
describe Susa in Neh. 1:1 and Esth. 1:2,5, etc). Jerusalem's citadel was close to the temple (cf. Neh. 2:8),
possibly incorporating the towers, the Hundred and Hananel (cf. Neh. 3:1). The same word "fortress" (BDB 108)
was used of the temple itself in 1 Chr. 29:1,19.

NASB, NRSV
"he was a faithful man"

NKJV
"he was a faithful man"

TEV
"Hananiah was a reliable"

NJB, JPSOA
"he was a more trustworthy"

Peshitta
"he was an upright man"

The term (BDB 54) for "faith" in the OT has the connotation of

- reliability, sureness (e.g., "the right way," Gen. 24:48)

- stability, continuance, faithfulness (e.g., Neh. 7:2; Isa. 38:3)

- truth (e.g., Esth. 9:30; Jer. 33:6)

This same term is often used of God (e.g., Neh. 9:33; Exod. 34:6; Isa. 38:18,19; Zech. 8:8).

Special Topic: Believe, Trust,
Faith, and Faithfulness in the OT

▣ "feared God more than many" This term (BDB 431, KB 432, Qal PERFECT [OT
Parsing Guide, p. 380], but Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE [Analytical Key to OT, p. 69]) is
used several times in Nehemiah and in several senses.

- Qal form

- fear God, Neh. 1:11; 7:2

- fear men, Neh. 2:2; 4:14; 6:13

- Niphal form ‒ God as awesome/fearful, Neh. 1:5; 4:14; 9:32

- the NOUN, fear of God, Neh. 5:9,15

Effective leaders are those who are trustworthy and revere YHWH!

Special Topic: Fear (OT)

verses.zh: 我吩咐他们说：「等到太阳上升才可开耶路撒冷的城门；人尚看守的时候就要关门上闩；也当派耶路撒冷的居民各按班次看守自己房屋对面之处。」
verses.en: I[NOTE:1] said to them, “The gates of Jerusalem must not be opened in the early morning,[NOTE:2] until those who are standing guard close the doors and lock them.[NOTE:3] Position residents of Jerusalem as guards, some at their guard stations and some near their homes.”
notes: The present translation (along with most English versions) reads with the Qere, a Qumran text, and the ancient versions וָאֹמַר (vaʾomar, “and I said”) rather than the Kethib of the MT, which reads וַיֹּאמֶר (vayyoʾmer, “and he said”).

Heb “until the heat of the sun.” The phrase probably means that the gates were to be opened only after the day had progressed a bit, not at the first sign of morning light (cf. KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV, TEV, CEV). It is possible, however, that the Hebrew preposition עַד (ʿad), here translated as “until,” has a more rare sense of “during.” If so, this would mean that the gates were not to be left open and unattended during the hot part of the day when people typically would be at rest (cf. NLT).

Presumably this would mean the gates were not to be opened until later in the morning and were to remain open until evening. Some, however, have understood Nehemiah’s instructions to mean that the gates were not to be left open during the hottest part of the day, but must be shut and locked while the guards are still on duty. See J. Barr, “Hebrew עַד, especially at Job i.18 and Neh vii.3, ” JJS 27 (1982): 177-88.
verses.commentary:
7:3 This verse has two IMPERFECTS used in a JUSSIVE sense ("be opened,"
"shut") and one IMPERATIVE ("bolt").

- The New English Bible and REV think it refers to closing the gates during the noon time rest

- the RSV, TEV, and NJB imply that the gates were to be opened late (well after sunrise) and closed
early (well before sundown)

- the UBS Text Project, p. 533, suggests "as long as (the people) are (still) up (i.e., have not yet
gone to bed)"

Whatever the specifics of this verse mean, it is obvious that special care was given to the opening,
closing, and guarding of Jerusalem's gates during this period.

Notice how the residents and businesses were to guard the entrances closest to their homes and
shops. This is the same personal interest used to construct the walls. The NIV and the NET Bibles understand
this aspect to relate to the separate guard stations, one at the gates and one by their homes.

verses.zh: 城是广大，其中的民却稀少，房屋还没有建造。
verses.en: Now the city was spread out[NOTE:1] and large, and there were not a lot of people in it.[NOTE:2] At that time houses had not been rebuilt.
notes: Heb “wide of two hands.”
Heb “the people were few in its midst.”
verses.commentary:
7:4 "the city was large and spacious" This is exactly opposite of the new size of the reduced city. What
can this mean?

- it must relate to the number of people living there, not a comparison of the previous size of the city

- there was plenty of room for new houses and shops (an invitation for people to move into the city)

Remember context, not lexicons, determine word meaning!

verses.zh: 我的　神感动我心，招聚贵胄、官长，和百姓，要照家谱计算。我找着第一次上来之人的家谱，其上写着：
verses.en: My God placed it on my heart to gather the leaders,[NOTE:1] the officials, and the ordinary people so they could be enrolled on the basis of genealogy. I found the genealogical records[NOTE:2] of those who had formerly returned. Here is what I found written in that record:[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “nobles”; NCV “important men.”
Heb “the book of genealogy.”
Heb “in it”; the referent (the genealogical record) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
verses.commentary: 7:5 Nehemiah felt he was led by YHWH.

verses.zh: 巴比伦王尼布甲尼撒从前掳去犹大省的人，现在他们的子孙从被掳到之地回耶路撒冷和犹大，各归本城。
verses.en: These are the people[NOTE:1] of the province who returned[NOTE:2] from the captivity of the exiles, whom King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon had forced into exile.[NOTE:3] They returned to Jerusalem and to Judah, each to his own city.
notes: Heb “the sons of”; KJV, ASV “the children of”; NAB “the inhabitants of.”
Heb “who were going up.”
One medieval Hebrew manuscript has “to Babylon.” Cf. Ezra 2:1.
verses.commentary:
7:6 "each to his city" This links up with Neh. 7:73a ("all Israel lived in their cities"). This was
important because Nehemiah divided the responsibilities for building and wall construction (and guarding and
protecting) by

- original city of the returnees' parents

- residence in Jerusalem

- guild/trade

- tribe (Levites, priests)

7:7a These are the main leaders and families.

▣ "Azariah" In Ezra 2:2 this is replaced by "Seraiah," in I Esdras 5:8, "Zaraias."

▣ "Raamiah" In Ezra 2:2 this is spelled Reelaiah; in I Esdras 5:9, Resaias.

▣ "Mispereth" In Ezra 2:2 this is spelled Mispar; it is not in I Esdras.

▣ "Nehum" In Ezra 2:2 this is replaced by Rehum; it is not in I Esdras.

verses.zh: 他们是同着所罗巴伯、耶书亚、尼希米、亚撒利雅、拉米、拿哈玛尼、末底改、必珊、米斯毗列、比革瓦伊、尼宏、巴拿回来的。
verses.en: They came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, and Baanah.The number of Israelite men[NOTE:1] was as follows:
notes: Heb “the men of the people of Israel.” Some English versions translate as “the people from Israel” (NCV) or “the Israelite people” (NRSV), but “men” should be retained because the following numbers presumably include only adult males.

verses.zh: 以色列人民的数目记在下面：巴录的子孙二千一百七十二名；
verses.en: the descendants[NOTE:1] of Parosh: 2,172;
notes: Heb “the sons of.”
verses.commentary: 7:8 "Parosh, 2,172" In I Esdras 5:9 it is "Phoros 2,172."

verses.zh: 示法提雅的子孙三百七十二名；
verses.en: the descendants of Shephatiah: 372;
verses.commentary: 7:9 "Shephatiah, 372" In I Esdras 5:10 it is "Saphat, 472."

verses.zh: 亚拉的子孙六百五十二名；
verses.en: the descendants of Arah: 652;
verses.commentary:
7:10 "Arah, 652" In I Esdras 5:10 it is "Ares, 756."

▣ "652" In Ezra 2:5 the number is 775.

verses.zh: 巴哈・摩押的后裔，就是耶书亚和约押的子孙二千八百一十八名；
verses.en: the descendants of Pahath Moab (from the line[NOTE:1] of Jeshua and Joab): 2,818;
notes: Heb “to the sons of.”

verses.zh: 以拦的子孙一千二百五十四名；

verses.zh: 萨土的子孙八百四十五名；

verses.zh: 萨改的子孙七百六十名；
verses.en: the descendants of Zaccai: 760;
verses.commentary: 7:14 "Zaccia, 760" I Esdras 5:13 has "Chorbe, 705."

verses.zh: 宾内的子孙六百四十八名；
verses.en: the descendants of Binnui: 648;

7:15 "Bennui" In Ezra 2:10 this is spelled Bani (as it is in I Esdras 5:13). The number of returnees

verses.zh: 比拜的子孙六百二十八名；
verses.en: the descendants of Bebai: 628;
verses.commentary: 7:16 "628" In Ezra 2:11 the number is 623.

verses.zh: 押甲的子孙二千三百二十二名；
verses.en: the descendants of Azgad: 2,322;
verses.commentary: 7:17 "Azgad, 2,322" In Ezra 2:12 the number is 1,222. In I Esdras 5:13 it is "Astad, 1,322."

verses.zh: 亚多尼干的子孙六百六十七名；
verses.en: the descendants of Adonikam: 667;
verses.commentary: 7:18 "667" In Ezra 2:13 the number is 666.

verses.zh: 比革瓦伊的子孙二千零六十七名；

verses.en: the descendants of Adin: 655;
verses.commentary: 7:20 "Adin, 655" In Ezra 2:15 the number is 454; in I Esdras 5:14 it is "Adinu, 454."

verses.zh: 哈顺的子孙三百二十八名；
verses.en: the descendants of Hashum: 328;
verses.commentary: 7:22 "Hashum 328" In Ezra this name appears in Neh. 2:19 and the number is 223.

verses.zh: 比赛的子孙三百二十四名；
verses.en: the descendants of Bezai: 324;
verses.commentary: 7:23 "Bezai, 324" In Ezra 2:17 the number is 323; in I Esdras 5:16 it is "Bassia, 323."

verses.zh: 哈拉的子孙一百一十二名；
verses.en: the descendants of Harif: 112;
verses.commentary: 7:24 "Hariph, 112" In Ezra 2:18 this is replaced by "Jorah, 112; in I Esdras 5:17 it is "Arsiphorith, 102."

verses.zh: 基遍人九十五名；
verses.en: the descendants of Gibeon: 95;
verses.commentary: 7:25 Gibeon" In Ezra 2:20 this is spelled Gibbar.

verses.zh: 伯利恒人和尼陀法人共一百八十八名；
verses.en: The men of Bethlehem[NOTE:1] and Netophah: 188;
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map7-E2; Map8-E2; Map10-B4.
verses.commentary:
7:26 Nehemiah's list combines the two cities with one number, 188, while Ezra 2:21-22 has 123 plus
56 which equals 179; I Esdras 5:17-18 has 123 plus 55 equaling 178.

verses.zh: 亚拿突人一百二十八名；
verses.en: the men of Anathoth: 128;

verses.zh: 伯・亚斯玛弗人四十二名；
verses.en: the men of the family[NOTE:1] of Azmaveth: 42;
notes: The translation reads בְּנֵי (bene, “the sons of”) rather than the MT reading אַנְשֵׁי בֵית (ʾanshe vet, “men of the house of”). Cf. Ezra 2:24.
verses.commentary:
7:28 "Beth-azmaveth" In Ezra 2:24 this is replaced simply by Azmaveth. Beth was a common addition to city
names ("house of," cf. Neh. 7:26). The NET Bible (p. 732) has "the family of Azmaveth," which is probably the
sense intended.

verses.zh: 基列・耶琳人、基非拉人、比录人共七百四十三名；
verses.en: the men of Kiriath Jearim, Kephirah, and Beeroth: 743;
verses.commentary: 7:29 "Kiriath-jearim" In Ezra 2:25 this is spelled Kiriath-arim"; in I Esdras 5:19 it is "Kariathiarius."

verses.zh: 拉玛人和迦巴人共六百二十一名；
verses.en: the men of Ramah and Geba: 621;

verses.zh: 默玛人一百二十二名；
verses.en: the men of Micmash: 122;

verses.zh: 伯特利人和艾人共一百二十三名；
verses.en: the men of Bethel[NOTE:1] and Ai: 123;
notes: For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.
verses.commentary:
7:32 "Ai" This is the city mentioned in Jos. 7-8.

▣ "123" In Ezra 2:28 the number is 223.

verses.zh: 别的尼波人五十二名；
verses.en: the men of the other Nebo: 52;
verses.commentary:
7:33 "the men of the other Nebo 52" "The other" is left out in Ezra 2:29. In Ezra 2:30 "sons of Magbish"
appears, but is left out in Nehemiah.

verses.zh: 别的以拦子孙一千二百五十四名；
verses.en: the descendants of the other Elam: 1,254;

verses.zh: 哈琳的子孙三百二十名；
verses.en: the descendants of Harim: 320;

verses.zh: 耶利哥人三百四十五名；
verses.en: the descendants of Jericho: 345;

verses.zh: 罗德人、哈第人、阿挪人共七百二十一名；
verses.en: the descendants of Lod, Hadid, and Ono: 721;
verses.commentary: 7:37 "721" Ezra 2:33 has the number 725. Also "the men of Jericho" in Ezra 2:34 is left out of Nehemiah.

verses.zh: 西拿人三千九百三十名。
verses.en: the descendants of Senaah: 3,930;
verses.commentary: 7:38 "3,930" In Ezra 2:35 the number is 3,630.

notes: Heb “to the house of.”
verses.commentary:
7:39 "Jedaiah of the house of Jeshua, 973" Ezra 2 has the same, but I Esdras 5:24 has "Jeddu, the son
of Jesus, among the sons of Sanasib, 972."

verses.zh: 音麦的子孙一千零五十二名；
verses.en: the descendants of Immer: 1,052;
verses.commentary: 7:40 "the sons of Immer, 1,052" Ezra 2 has the same, but I Esdras 5:24 has "the sons of Emmeruth, 1,052."

verses.zh: 巴施户珥的子孙一千二百四十七名；
verses.en: the descendants of Pashhur: 1,247;
verses.commentary: 7:41 "the sons of Pashhus, 1,247" Ezra 2 has the same, but I Esdras 5:25 has "the sons of Phassurus, 1,246."

verses.zh: 哈琳的子孙一千零一十七名。
verses.en: the descendants of Harim: 1,017.
verses.commentary: 7:42 "the sons of Harin, 1,017" Ezra 2 has the same, but I Esdras 5:25 has "the sons of Charme, 1,017."

verses.zh: 利未人：何达威的后裔，就是耶书亚和甲篾的子孙七十四名。

verses.commentary:
7:43 "Hodevah" In Ezra 2:40 this is spelled "Hodariah." This name is not found in I Esdras 5:26; it has
"Bannas and Sudias."

verses.zh: 歌唱的：亚萨的子孙一百四十八名。
verses.en: The singers: the descendants of Asaph: 148.
verses.commentary:
7:44 "Asaph" He was appointed by David as Levitical musician (cf. 1 Chr. 25; 2 Chr. 25:12). He became the
head of a family of musicians (cf. Ezra 2:41; 3:10; Neh. 11:17,22; 12:35).

▣ "148" In Ezra 2:41 the number is 128 (as it is in I Esdras 5:27).

verses.zh: 守门的：沙龙的子孙、亚特的子孙、达们的子孙、亚谷的子孙、哈底大的子孙、朔拜的子孙，共一百三十八名。
verses.en: The gatekeepers: the descendants of Shallum, the descendants of Ater, the descendants of Talmon, the descendants of Akkub, the descendants of Hatita, and the descendants of Shobai: 138.
verses.commentary: 7:45 "138" In Ezra 2:45 the number is 139 (as it is in I Esdras 5:28).

verses.zh: 尼提宁（就是殿役）：西哈的子孙、哈苏巴的子孙、答巴俄的子孙、
verses.en: The temple servants: the descendants of Ziha, the descendants of Hasupha, the descendants of Tabbaoth,

verses.zh: 基绿的子孙、西亚的子孙、巴顿的子孙、
verses.en: the descendants of Keros, the descendants of Sia, the descendants of Padon,
verses.commentary: 7:47 "Sia" In Ezra 2:44 this is spelled Siaha; in I Esdras 5:29, "Sua."

verses.zh: 利巴拿的子孙、哈迦巴的子孙、萨买的子孙、
verses.en: the descendants of Lebanah, the descendants of Hagabah, the descendants of Shalmai,
verses.commentary:
7:48 "the sons of Lebana, ths sons of Hagaba, the sons of Shalmai" In Ezra 2:45 the first two names have
a concluding "h" and the last name is replaced by "Akkub." Nehemiah's list seems to omit Hagab. These two names,
"Hagabah" and "Hagab," found in Ezra 2:45-46, are easily confused. The list is quite different and abbreviated
in I Esdras.

verses.zh: 哈难的子孙、吉德的子孙、迦哈的子孙、
verses.en: the descendants of Hanan, the descendants of Giddel, the descendants of Gahar,

verses.zh: 利亚雅的子孙、利汛的子孙、尼哥大的子孙、
verses.en: the descendants of Reaiah, the descendants of Rezin, the descendants of Nekoda,

verses.zh: 迦散的子孙、乌撒的子孙、巴西亚的子孙、

verses.zh: 所罗门仆人的后裔，就是琐太的子孙、琐斐列的子孙、比路大的子孙、
verses.en: The descendants of the servants of Solomon: the descendants of Sotai, the descendants of Sophereth, the descendants of Perida,
verses.commentary:
7:57 "Sophereth" In Ezra 2:55 it is spelled Hassophereth; I Esdras 5:33 has "Assaphioth." This word

verses.zh: 雅拉的子孙、达昆的子孙、吉德的子孙、

verses.commentary:

verses.en: All the temple servants and the descendants of the servants of Solomon, 392.

verses.zh: 从特米拉、特哈萨、基绿、亚顿、音麦上来的，不能指明他们的宗族谱系是以色列人不是；
verses.en: These are the ones who came up from Tel Melah, Tel Harsha, Kerub, Addon, and Immer (although they were unable to certify[NOTE:1] their family connection[NOTE:2] or their ancestry,[NOTE:3] as to whether they were really from Israel):
notes: Heb “relate.”
Heb “the house of their fathers.”
Heb “their seed.”

verses.zh: 他们是第莱雅的子孙、多比雅的子孙、尼哥大的子孙，共六百四十二名。
verses.en: the descendants of Delaiah, the descendants of Tobiah, and the descendants of Nekoda, 642.
verses.commentary: 7:62 "642" In Ezra 2:60 the number is 652.

verses.zh: 祭司中，哈巴雅的子孙、哈哥斯的子孙、巴西莱的子孙；因为他们的先祖娶了基列人巴西莱的女儿为妻，所以起名叫巴西莱。
verses.en: And from among the priests: the descendants of Hobaiah, the descendants of Hakkoz, and the descendants of Barzillai (who had married a woman from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by that name).
verses.commentary: 7:63 "Hobaiaha" Ezra 2:61 spells the name "Habaiah."

verses.zh: 这三家的人在族谱之中寻查自己的谱系，却寻不着，因此算为不洁，不准供祭司的职任。
verses.en: They searched for their records in the genealogical materials, but none were found. They were therefore excluded[NOTE:1] from the priesthood.
notes: Heb “they were desecrated.”
verses.commentary:
7:64 "they were considered unclean" The VERB (BDB 146 II, KB 169, Pual
IMPERFECT) means "defiled," here in the same sense that their Levitical ancestry could not be
confirmed. The special food for the priests could not be eaten by them (cf. Lev. 2:3; 7:21-36) because they were
undocumented.

verses.zh: 省长对他们说：「不可吃至圣的物，直到有用乌陵和土明决疑的祭司兴起来。」
verses.en: The governor[NOTE:1] instructed them not to eat any of the sacred food until there was a priest who could consult[NOTE:2] the Urim and Thummim.
notes: The Hebrew term תִּרְשָׁתָא (tirshataʾ; KJV “Tirshatha”) is the official title of a Persian governor in Judea. In meaning it may be similar to “excellency” (cf. NAB). See further BDB 1077 s.v.; W. L. Holladay, Concise Hebrew and Aramaic Lexicon, 395; HALOT 1798 s.v.
Heb “stood.”
verses.commentary:
7:65 "The governor" refers to Nehemiah (Ezra 2:63, "Tirshatha"; I Esdras 5:40 has "Nehemias" and
"Attharias"). He demanded that their confirmation be a heavenly affirmation. The Urim and Thummim were a
set of objects (cf. Exod. 28:30; Lev. 8:8) kept by the High Priest (cf. Deut. 33:8) used to determine the will
of God (cf. Num. 27:21). Nehemiah seems to be using

- these objects

- and a future priest as a way of referring to God's Promised One (much like Zechariah used Joshua)

Special Topic: Urim and Thummim

verses.zh: 会众共有四万二千三百六十名。
verses.en: The entire group numbered 42,360—
verses.commentary:
7:66 "42,360" This same number is also in Ezra 2:64. When you add up both Ezra's (29,818) and Nehemiah's
(31,089) lists by names, cities and groups neither equal this number. This shows that both lists are incomplete.

Milton Terry, Biblical Hermeneutics, p. 525, has an interesting numerical comment.

"The probability is that neither list is intended as a perfect enumeration of all the
families that returned from exile, but only of such families of Judah and Benjamin as could show an authentic
genealogy of their father's house, while the 42,360 includes many persons and families belonging to other
tribes who in their exile had lost all certain record of their genealogy, but were nevertheless true descendants
of some of the ancient tribes. It is also noticeable that Ezra's list mentions 494 persons not recognized
in Nehemiah's list, and Nehemiah's list mentions 1,765 not recognised in Ezra's list; but if we add the
surplus of Ezra to the sum of Nehemiah (494 + 31,089 = 31,583) we have the same result as by adding Nehemiah's
surplus to the sums of Ezra's numbers (1,765 + 29,818 = 31,583). Hence it may be reasonably believed
that 31,583 was the sum of all that could show their father's house, that the two lists were drawn up
independently of each other; and that both are defective, though one supplies the defects of the other."

verses.zh: 此外，还有他们的仆婢七千三百三十七名，又有歌唱的男女二百四十五名。
verses.en: not counting their 7,337 male and female servants. They also had 245 male and female singers.
verses.commentary:
7:67 "245" In Ezra 2:65 the number of singers is 200; I Esdras 5:42 also has "245."

The UBS Text Project. p. 534, has the following comment:

Although the MT of Nehemiah is not original here, it cannot be replaced by another more original
text form. For there is no ancient textual witness which attests to such a more original text than the MT. The parallel
passage in Ezra 2.65-66 shows that the original Nehemiah text has been lost through homoeoteleuton, and it is from
here that certain Hebrew manuscripts and old and modern translations complete the Nehemiah text."

verses.zh: 他们有马七百三十六匹，骡子二百四十五匹，
verses.en: They had 736 horses, 245 mules,
verses.commentary: 7:68 Many Hebrew manuscripts omit this verse, as does the Septuagint. However, it is present in Ezra 2:66.

verses.zh: 骆驼四百三十五只，驴六千七百二十匹。
verses.en: (7:68)[NOTE:1] 435 camels, and 6,720 donkeys.
notes: Most Hebrew MSS omit 7:68 ET, which reads “They had 736 horses, 245 mules,” and thus have one less verse in chap. 7, ending the chapter at 7:72. This verse is included in the LXX and most English versions. Cf. Ezra 2:66.
verses.commentary:
7:69 The numbers between Ezra and Nehemiah are very different. See John H. Walton and D. Brent Sandy,
The Lost World of Scripture, which discusses how oral cultures pass on their traditions.

verses.en: What the rest of the people gave amounted to 20,000 gold drachmas, 2,000 silver minas, and 67 priestly garments.

verses.zh: 于是祭司、利未人、守门的、歌唱的、民中的一些人、尼提宁，并以色列众人，各住在自己的城里。
verses.en: The priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, some of the people, the temple servants, and all the rest of Israel lived in their cities.When the seventh month arrived and the Israelites[NOTE:1] were settled in their towns,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the sons of Israel.” So also in vv. 14, 17; 9:1.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

A. This list is very similar to the list of Ezra 2 ("those who came up first," Neh. 7:5, also note I Esdras 5:8-42).

B. The names were probably originally based on the same official list (Persian or Jewish), but they are not exactly the same. Names are spelled differently and some names are added and omitted. The stated numbers also do not always agree.

C. The list is divided into categories of people:

1. men of Israel, Neh. 7:7b-38

2. priests, Neh. 7:39-42

3. Levites, Neh. 7:43-45

4. temple servants, Neh. 7:46-56

5. sons of Solomon's slaves, Neh. 7:57-60

6. those of undocumentable ancestry, Neh. 7:61-65

a. laymen, Neh. 7:61-62

b. priests, Neh. 7:63

D. Summaries

1. of those who returned, Neh. 7:66-67

2. of the offerings, Neh. 7:70-72

a. Persian

b. Jewish

E. See notes at Ezra 2 on specific names and categories of returnees

F. I Esdras (also knows as Esdras A) is a Greek version of Josiah's Passover (2 Chr. 35,36) through Nehemiah 7 (which is paralleled in Ezra 2). It differs from the MT and the LXX. For a good brief discussion see R. K. Harrison, Introduction to the Old Testament, pp. 1194-1199.
